records.summary: Vietnam's central bank has no statutory power to set its own policy target. Article 2 of the Law on the State Bank of Vietnam No. 46/2010/QH12, passed on 16 June 2010 and in force from 1 January 2011, makes the State Bank a ministerial-level agency of the Government as well as the central bank. Article 3 gives the National Assembly the power to decide the annual inflation rate target and to oversee implementation of national monetary policy, with the Government proposing that target to it; the Prime Minister or the Governor then decides on the use of administrative tools and measures, following the Government's own regulations. This is a standing arrangement with no end date and no episode attached: the bank implements a target set above it rather than being pressed on any particular occasion.
records.source_title: Consolidated Text 25/VBHN-VPQH 2022 of the Law on the State Bank of Vietnam, articles 2 and 3 (Office of the National Assembly)

records.summary: The Bulgarian National Bank published a letter it had received from the European Central Bank, signed by ECB president Mario Draghi, warning that proposed amendments to Bulgaria's deposit insurance legislation could infringe the central bank's independence. The amendments would have obliged the BNB to cover any shortfall in the Bulgarian Deposit Guarantee Fund's resources. The ECB's objections as reported were that the draft would stop the BNB investing and managing its own reserves, that provisional transfers to the Deposit Insurance Fund could severely limit the bank's own resources and reserves and so hinder the tasks it carries out within the European System of Central Banks, and that such a transfer could put the stability of Bulgaria's currency board at risk. The Bulgarian News Agency BTA, reporting the same opinion on the same day, quotes it as finding that the draft law impairs the institutional and financial independence of the BNB and may also impair its functional independence.
records.source_title: ECB: Proposed Changes to Bulgaria Deposit Insurance Law Harm C-Bank (Novinite, 10 December 2014)

records.move: from Director of the Research Department of the Bank of Guyana to Alternate Executive Director at the World Bank in Washington, and back to the bank as Deputy Governor ; from Deputy Governor to Governor
records.summary: The Bank of Guyana's governor profile page gives Gobind Ganga's full career. He was Director of the bank's Research Department from 1995 until November 2003, when he was appointed Alternate Executive Director at the World Bank in Washington, D.C.; he returned to the bank as Deputy Governor in June 2005 after that term ended, and became Governor on 2 December 2014. His earlier posts were academic, at the University of the West Indies at Mona in Jamaica, the Consortium Graduate School at Mona and the University of Guyana. No private employer appears anywhere in the career the bank publishes, and no part of it is in finance outside the public sector: the only outside institution is the World Bank.

records.central_bank: National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia
records.move: from manager of the Treasury Department and State Secretary at the Ministry of Finance, and economist in the IMF's European Department, to Vice-Governor and then Governor of the National Bank
records.summary: The National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia's governor page gives Anita Angelovska Bezhoska's full career. At the Ministry of Finance she was an expert associate on the financial system, then head of the project to establish a treasury system, then manager of the Treasury Department, about eight years in total, and State Secretary in 2003 and 2004. At the International Monetary Fund she was an economist in the European Department for about two years and briefly in the Fiscal Affairs Department in Washington, and has served on IMF technical assistance teams for European countries since 2006. She joined the bank as Chief Economist, served almost eight years as Vice-Governor for monetary policy, research and statistics, and became Governor in May 2018. The page names no private firm and no commercial bank: every employer in it is a state body or an international organisation.
records.source_title: Governor Anita Angelovska Bezhoska, National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia
